subject: Feature binning + safepoints — decision framework and migration checkpoints
messages:
From: Claire Holt <claire@novomed.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: Jamal Reeves <jamal.reeves@novomed.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Choosing the right bundle — upgrade vs. add-on approach

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked great and the support SLA is promising. We're huddling on packaging now and I wanted to get your help on two questions before we present to procurement: 

1) We currently expect to roll Redwood across 3 product teams over the next 12 months. Each team will have distinct feature needs: realtime chat, nightly batch embeddings, and a search rerank route. Does it make sense to take a single higher-tier package and gate features per-team, or buy separate smaller packages per team and use add-on units for cross-team features?

2) For upgrade safety: if we start with a compact tier and need to move to a throughput-first tier in Q3, what's your process for an in-flight migration and rollback safepoint? We need a clear checklist for procurement and engineering to sign off.

Attached: a short summary of our current usage assumptions and a spreadsheet of peak/avg token estimates.

Appreciate a short decision-oriented note we can include in the RFP.

— Claire
Claire Holt
Head of Platform Integrations, Novomed Health
[Attachment: novomed-usage-estimates.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)]

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: Claire Holt <claire@novomed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Choosing the right bundle — upgrade vs. add-on approach

Claire —

Thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise decision framework you can paste into the RFP and a migration safepoint checklist for procurement/engineering. I'll keep it short so your team can slot it in.

Decision framework (pasteable):
- If cross-team feature parity matters (shared prompts, consistent QA/evals) → prefer single higher-tier with per-route feature flags.
- If teams are organizationally independent and you want billing granularity → prefer separate smaller packages + shared add-on pool for burst/overage.
- If you need predictable unit economics for high-throughput routes (search rerank) → dedicate throughput units (reserved capacity) for that route and keep others on metered host.

Migration & rollback safepoints (abbrev):
1) Pre-migration: baseline latency and token-cost report (7d), run a mini-canary with 5% traffic on target tier.
2) Data configuration: ensure model pinning & KV cache warmup plan, export eval prompts and expected BLEU/regression checks.
3) Cutover window: schedule a 2-hour low-traffic window, enable mirrored traffic, observe 15-minute SLO trend.
4) Safepoint: create billing snapshot and config tag, and hold an automatic rollback trigger if tail latency or error rate > 3x baseline for 10 minutes.
5) Post-migration: 24h reconciliation run, exchange final usage numbers and pro-rate adjustments if upgrade confirmed.

Attachments I recommend for your procurement packet: our one-page pricing summary (attached), and a short amendment template for minor seat/throughput changes. Ben — adding you in case you want to propose a limited-time step-up discount for initial multi-team rollouts.

Let me know if you want this reworded for legal/vendor language.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire@novomed.com>, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Choosing the right bundle — upgrade vs. add-on approach

Claire — quick note from pricing:

We can offer a hybrid path to reduce procurement friction:
- Start: compact team packages for each product team (3x compact) + a shared 50k-token/month add-on pool.
- Step-up: include a one-time convertible credit equal to 10% of the first 3 months' committed spend that can be applied to an annual reserved-throughput commitment within 90 days of rollout.
- Rollback protection: during a priced step-up we can include a 30-day change window with pro-rated credits if you need to reverse to the compact tier.

If you prefer a single enterprise package we can discount the annual commitment by 7% and include dedicated throughput for the rerank route. Option pricing attached — see page 2 for the convertible credit example.

Next step: if that sounds reasonable, can we schedule a 30-minute procurement alignment call next week to run the RFP language and confirm contract terms? I put a proposed agenda at the bottom.

Agenda (30m):
- Confirm decision framework language (5m)
- Walk through pricing options & convertible credit mechanic (10m)
- Migration safepoint checklist & support model during cutover (10m)
- Next steps / legal contacts (5m)

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, GTM Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: novomed-amendment-draft-20270518.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: Claire Holt <claire@novomed.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jamal Reeves <jamal.reeves@novomed.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Choosing the right bundle — upgrade vs. add-on approach

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick replies: 
- The hybrid path sounds like the least friction for procurement. The convertible credit mechanic should be spelled out in the RFP (how it's earned, how it converts).
- For safepoints we'll ask engineering to sign the rollback trigger thresholds; your 3x tail-latency threshold seems reasonable but we'll confirm with our infra team.
- Request: can you add an explicit line about support during cutover (on-call engineer, post-cutover 24h war room, one dedicated runbook update)? We'll include that in the SOW appendix.

Let's take your agenda — can you send 3 slots next week? I'll loop Legal after the call.

— Claire
Claire Holt
Head of Platform Integrations, Novomed Health
